attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: The function takes no parameter and reads no table, so no text input exists.

collation-case.notApplicableReason: No text input and no text comparison.

dates-datetime.notApplicableReason: No date input: the only dates are constants inside the function. The datetime 3.33 ms rounding of DATEADD(millisecond, -2, ...) is attacked through the result value (A01).

numeric-rounding.notApplicableReason: No decimal or money input or result.

top-ties.notApplicableReason: Scalar function: returns one value, no rows from tables.

identity-gaps.notApplicableReason: Reads no table, no key or sequence.

cases.label: midnight minus 2 ms on datetime: the result is the .997 tick, kept at 3 digits (not .998, not rounded to the second)
cases.reasoning: T-SQL DATEADD(millisecond, -2, datetime '2004-07-01') lands on the datetime tick .997 (3.33 ms resolution). PostgreSQL interval arithmetic would give .998; the conversion hard-codes .997 and returns timestamp(3). A timestamp(0) or a date return type, or the exact -2 ms, would differ from the value SQL Server returns.

objections.text: A01 sends the same complete payload as the sole hand-derived fixed case: no arguments and no tables. Both cases assert the same .997 datetime result and type, so A01 adds no distinct attack input.

caught: end date is exactly 2 ms before midnight (datetime would give .997)
